newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-BOLD BEVAN SHINES AS AUSTRALIA SCORE 219-7.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BOLD BEVAN SHINES AS AUSTRALIA SCORE 219-7.

text.p: Michael Bevan hit 56 as Australia scored 219 for seven in their 50 overs against South Africa in a one-day triangular series on Saturday.
Taylor and Waugh gave Australia a good start, putting on 85 for the first wicket, but the middle-order batting collapsed, with four wickets falling for 21 runs.
Taylor survived two dropped catches, one by Brian McMillan off paceman Allan Donald and one by Donald off off-spinner Pat Symcox.
He was eventually run out for 39 by a throw by Derek Crookes from mid-wicket when he was looking for a second run.
Mark Waugh scored 50 runs off 66 balls, including five fours, before he too was run out. Jonty Rhodes, alert at mid-wicket, dismissed the Australian who was caught in two minds looking for a single.

Waugh's twin brother Steve was stumped by Dave Richardson trying to hit a flighted ball from Symcox and Stuart Law was caught and bowled by off-spinner Crookes in the next over. Each made only one run.
Ricky Ponting, with a patient 35, and Bevan perked up the innings with a 61-run stand before Ponting was caught behind as he slashed at Donald.
Bevan, whose innings lasted 78 balls, hit six fours including two in one over from paceman Brian McMillan whose bowling came in for some punishment.
Bevan was out in the 49th over, his leg stump uprooted by Donald, who next dismissed Ian Healy for 12 and finished with figures of three for 57.
Healy was caught off his glove at backward point by Rhodes, who dived brilliantly to his left and plucked the ball off the ground.
